item.title: Six Weeks in One Night: How a Product Gets Built in the Agentic Era
item.description: I gave a human development plan to a team of agents, an Opus spec writer, a Sonnet developer and an Opus reviewer, and let them build the first phase of Graft overnight. Six planned weeks became one night, at about 0.5% of the human cost. But the bottleneck didn’t disappear. It moved to us.

item.title: Use AI to Build the Tool, Not to Be the Tool
item.description: Asking an agent to block focus time, summarise yesterday’s numbers or find a meeting slot works, but you pay for it every time, and the answer changes. I measured 14 Claude Code runs on three everyday jobs. Writing the script once costs about as much as asking once. With an interactive calculator, a checklist, and my own projects as examples.

item.title: Drowning in Email: ai-email-assistant, Rules First, Models Last
item.description: A Gmail triage that costs cents. Deterministic rules handle the routine mail, Claude Haiku looks only at what’s left, Claude Sonnet only at what Haiku isn’t sure about, and code validates every answer. Requests become Google Tasks with a due date. With a real run on my inbox, a from-zero install with Homebrew, and a few thoughts on letting an AI answer your mail.
